candidates.source_title: Castleton house approved for eight-bed care home
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A house in Castleton can be turned into a care home for up to eight adults after Rochdale Council approved the plans on 18 November. The home at 9 Thornham New Road would provide 24-hour care. The plans include a new upstairs bay window and changes to the layout inside. The council received 20 comments on the application. People raised concerns about parking, noise and whether emergency vehicles could reach the home. Highways officers did not object. They said the home was unlikely to add much traffic and that its driveway had room for three or four cars. The council requires two spaces for a care home of this size. The applicant says there would be no more than two staff on site at a time, including during shift changes. A condition limits the home to eight residents and work must start within three years. candidates.source_title: Free health checks identify 1,000 undiagnosed conditions - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A community initiative which offers free health checks across Rochdale, Heywood and Middleton, has found that 50% of people didn’t know they needed medical attention. Launched on October 31, 2025, the free Community Health Checks programme, commissioned by Rochdale Council and delivered by the Living Well Rochdale Cardiovascular Disease (CVD) team, has reached an impressive milestone, with 2,000 health checks carried out across the borough. The initiative aims to make essential health screening more accessible, particularly for residents who may face difficulties accessing traditional GP services or who might not otherwise seek a routine health check. The initiative has seen the Living Well Rochdale CVD team take its services directly into the community, with checks carried out at a range of locations, including community venues, GP practices, workplaces, places of worship and even local cash-and-carry stores. Each free health check includes blood pressure monitoring, height and weight measurements, and a simple finger-prick test to assess blood sugar and cholesterol levels. Residents also receive their Body Mass Index (BMI) and QRISK3 assessment, which helps estimate their risk of developing cardiovascular disease over the next ten years. These quick and convenient checks provide valuable information about an individual’s health, helping to identify potential concerns before they develop into more serious conditions. candidates.source_title: Dale ‘really enjoys’ playing for Cobblers after standout display
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The 28-year-old winger, who joined Town on a one-year deal at the end of the summer transfer window, produced another excellent performance and was on target with a well-taken finish after 11 minutes. “I’ve started to get into a bit of a rhythm now and I’m building those relationships with other players in the team,” said Dale. “My main aim is just to help the team get us to where we want to get to. “I’ve got to credit the boys, I can’t play the way I play without them and what they do behind me, and obviously I’m happy with the goal. “I’ve had a few where I’ve been a bit unlucky and I’ve been critical of myself because I feel I could have had four or five already. But now that first one has gone in hopefully it opens the floodgates.” On how he’s finding life at Sixfields in general, Dale added: “I’m really enjoying myself. The group’s top, as are the manager and the staff, and the way we play really suits me. It allows me to express myself and I’m enjoying being part of this team.” Dale’s goal was the least Cobblers deserved for a dominant first half display but a wobble after half-time put the result in doubt - until Elliott List and Lee Evans turned things around. “It was really important to get the win and obviously I’m happy on a personal note to get off the mark,” Dale continued. “It’s been a few games coming but hopefully I can kick-on and score a few more. “I thought we showed great resilience and the lads did a great job off the bench. We are disappointed with how we started the second half because that should have been a 3-0 game, not 3-2, after how we played in the first half. “We will look back at that and we’ll be critical of ourselves but these things happen and the resilience we showed is a credit to the group and to the manager and the staff and how we’re building. We’re getting better and better.”
candidates.source_summary: Cobblers forward Owen Dale says he is ‘really enjoying’ his time at the club and hopes the ‘floodgates now open’ after scoring his first goal against Rochdale on Saturday.

candidates.source_title: Ian Watson leaves Rochdale after 3-2 defeat as search begins for new boss - Dave.Sport
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale have begun the search for Ian Watson’s successor after defeat at Northampton left Dale 22nd. Barnet visit Spotland on Saturday. Rochdale parted company with head coach Ian Watson on Sunday 22 November after a 3-2 defeat at Northampton Town left them 22nd in League Two. The club have begun the search for his successor ahead of Saturday’s home game against Barnet. In their statement on Sunday , Rochdale thanked Watson for his work at the Crown Oil Arena and said the recruitment process was already under way. He leaves five months after taking charge, with Dale two points clear of relegation and four wins from their opening 16 league games. Northampton and Rochdale began Saturday level on points. Two of the players he recalled to the starting line-up, Ed Francis and Cian Hayes, scored within two minutes of each other early in the second half to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. It lasted just 12 minutes. Elliott List equalised before Lee Evans converted the penalty that settled the game, leaving Dale to travel home without a point despite having led with half an hour to play. “We didn’t start the game well at all,” Watson told the club’s post-match interview on Saturday. His departure was announced the following morning. Ian Watson succeeded Jimmy McNulty in June after McNulty guided Rochdale back into the Football League and left for Stockport. The former South Shields manager did take Dale into the second round of the FA Cup , beating Fleetwood 2-1 away earlier this month. Two League Two fixtures come before the home cup tie against Newport on 5 December. Barnet visit first, followed by a trip to Cheltenham on Tuesday 1 December.

candidates.source_title: Hogg reveals ‘angriness’ in Cobblers dressing room despite Rochdale win
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Northampton completely dominated the first half at Sixfields and had chances to be home and dry well before the break. They racked up 15 shots to Dale’s three and forced visiting goalkeeper Sam Waller into a string of saves. But they only had Owen Dale’s 11th-minute opener to show for their efforts and the away side scored twice in three minutes to turn the game around at the start of the second half, before Elliott List and Lee Evans rescued victory. "Even at the end, there was real relief in the dressing room in terms of the result but also there was a bit of angriness about not having the game out of sight before they got back into it,” admitted Hogg. "But sometimes you need these experiences in life and in football and you need to go through the hardships to go and better. You don't want it every week but it's the first time in a long time that the team has come back and won and that bodes really well for the future.” Asked why Rochdale were allowed to get back into the game, Hogg said: "If I had the answer to that it wouldn't have happened. I felt we created some really good chances in the first half, we had lots of shots and our attacking metrics were really good, and 1-0 was the very least we deserved. “It was just the quality of the finish that let us down and we spoke about that at half-time. The game should have been over, but we changed the shape in the second half and managed to wrestle back the momentum. The boys puffed their chests out and came out with three points.” Dale produced another excellent individual performance and was rewarded with his first goal for the club, drilling into the bottom corner after just 11 minutes. "I'm delighted for Owen,” Hogg added. “He's been terrific behind the scenes in terms of his work-rate and everything he does. He deserved that goal. “He's been chasing it a little bit, both in training and in games, but he's had a big impact on us and he's a great lad to work with and I was so pleased to see him get his goal.”

candidates.source_title: New mental health football project kicks off in Rochdale
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A pioneering football-based project is helping young girls in Rochdale build confidence, friendships and resilience through the power of sport. Pennine Care NHS and Pennine Care Charity have teamed up with Rochdale AFC Community Trust to deliver a new programme for girls aged six to 11 who are waiting for, or already receiving, support from Rochdale child and adolescent mental health services (CAMHS). The free 36-week pilot uses fun football activities to help girls stay active and develop their confidence, social skills and emotional wellbeing in a safe and welcoming environment. The programme was developed following feedback from parents of children receiving support from CAMHS, who highlighted the need for activities to help their children build self-esteem and make friends. The project is funded by the Football Association’s Empower Her Fund, which supports opportunities for women and girls to get involved in football. Sessions are delivered by experienced staff from Rochdale AFC Community Trust. Sixteen girls have taken part so far, with early feedback showing how much they are enjoying the sessions and the opportunities to build confidence and make new friends. Anders Cox is clinical lead at Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale CAMHS, run by Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust. Anders said: “Getting active, making friends and feeling part of something can all support young people’s mental health. This project gives the girls a fun and welcoming environment where they can build their confidence, learn new skills and enjoy being active together.”

The Primary Engineer Vehicle Programme opens the door to real-world engineering: teachers and pupils meet and collaborate with engineering professionals, grow their creativity and technical skills and experience the excitement of building something to be proud of. Howard told police he had fatally stabbed Keeley two days earlier and was reporting the incident because her body was beginning to smell. When questioned, Howard said that the pair had been drinking and began to argue in the kitchen. Keeley was cooking at the time and had a knife in her hand as the pair began to “tussle”. Howard admitted he had his hands around Keeley’s neck and punched her, but he could not remember exactly how the knife ended up in Keeley’s chest, but he said it “just did”. A Home Office post-mortem exmination found that Keeley had suffered a stab wound to the chest, bruising to her neck consistent with strangulation and various other scratches and bruises on her body. Throughout the investigation, Greater Manchester Police’s Major Incident Team unravelled a pattern of domestic abuse from Howard toward Keeley.

candidates.source_title: The sun sets on Rochdale's Seven Sisters
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The sun appears to be setting on the famous Seven Sisters tower blocks in Rochdale . On Monday, Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) announced their intention to demolish the goliaths that have dominated the town’s skyline since the 1960s . They want to replace the 766 flats, most of which sit empty, with 601 new homes. The scheme would provide a mix of flats and townhouses - with a shift towards more family homes from a setup of mainly bedsits and one-beds. The Seven Sisters - actually named College Bank - have become part of the furniture. Lots of Rochdalians having either lived there, or had friends and family live there. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter To imagine travelling down the M62 and not seeing the brutalist siblings protruding into the sky seems odd. But it only takes one trip around the estate to realise the blocks have gotten into a sorry state. The garages below are all boarded up, rubbish is littered outside and the tower blocks themselves are becoming tatty, with signs visibly falling apart. RBH, who own the land, say they are becoming more unsafe - which is why two blocks have already been closed and the rest are currently being emptied. The decision to rehouse all 229 flats left occupied was made in October 2025 . Only 78 households remain, but they’re due to be out by next summer. Of those still left, there is a strong contingent of campaigners hoping to stop the demolition. The Save the Seven Sisters group (ST7S) want to see the blocks refurbished instead and have even come up with a plan on how to do it, but RBH don’t agree it’s feasible. Tenants have lived in limbo for a decade - ever since RBH originally announced their intention to demolish 10 years ago. RBH has shifted its stance multiple times - moving from part-demolition, to ruling it out entirely in 2023, before putting ‘all options back on the table’ in 2024, then finally deciding to demolish them this week. It has been a turbulent time to say the least. It could be argued that the situation is no further on than 10 years ago, but the picture in Rochdale has dramatically changed since. Former Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham put together a taskforce in 2024 to look into alternatives to demolition. The taskforce is made up of Rochdale council , the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA), the Rochdale MPs office, the Greater Manchester Tenants Union and RBH. candidates.source_title: Chris Hogg hails Northampton reaction against Rochdale - Central Fife Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Northampton boss Chris Hogg hailed the “outstanding reaction” of his players after they fought back from 2-1 down to beat Rochdale 3-2. Owen Dale gave the Cobblers an early lead at Sixfields but two goals in as many minutes from Ed Francis and Cian Hayes turned things around at the start of the second half. However, Elliott List levelled just after the hour-mark before Lee Evans won it from the penalty spot with 16 minutes to play. “It was a bit of a roller-coaster and it’s another experience for us as a team and as a group of people,” said Hogg. “We’ve already been through a lot of experiences this season, some good and some not so good, but I’m really pleased for the players today – I thought their reaction in the second half was outstanding. “The game should have been dead and buried for me in the first half. One goal was the very least we deserved and I spoke at half-time about being ruthless and then you blink and you’re 2-1 down and that’s a lesson for us. “You can’t wait to go 2-1 down to start playing again, but Listy came on and I thought he was terrific. “We changed the shape slightly and we wrestled the momentum back.

candidates.source_title: Opposition view: Rochdale boss felt penalty call was ‘really harsh’
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Kane Taylor was adjudged to have had his arm in an unnatural position when blocking Elliott List’s cross with 16 minutes to play. Referee Callum Jones took his time before pointing to the spot and Lee Evans made no mistake from 12 yards to complete Northampton’s comeback after Dale had found themselves 2-1 in front. Earlier, the home side dominated the first half and would have been out of sight if not for Sam Waller. The Rochdale goalkeeper made a series of saves both before and after Owen Dale’s opener. “We didn’t start the game well at all," admitted Watson. “The opposition got on top of us and deservedly took the lead. We came more into it later in the first half and did have a couple of chances before half-time. “We demanded more energy and more intensity in the second half and we got that and we scored the two goals, but I felt we then dropped off too much and gave them too much space. “But the penalty is really harsh. He’s falling back, the ball hits his hand from a very short distance and the ref takes a long time to think about it. It’s a tough one. “But there’s no papering over any cracks. We weren’t good enough to win the game and that’s because we didn’t start the game well enough. Our goalkeeper has made a couple of great saves and I felt we had a real fear and anxiety about getting on the ball and that’s not the team we want to be. “We wanted to change the mentality and mindset at half-time and come out on the front foot and the boys did really well to get back into the game. They did everything they could and they worked hard as hard as they could - that’s not the reason we didn’t win the game.”

candidates.source_title: Campaigners hit out at ‘absurd’ College Bank demolition decision - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Campaigners fighting to save Rochdale’s College Bank flats from demolition are calling on community leaders to step in and save the landmark tower blocks. Yesterday, Rochdale Boroughwide Housing announced that demolition and redevelopment of the site is the only viable option for the 61-year-old tower blocks known as the Seven Sisters. It said refurbishing them would cost at least £269 million and take up to 12 years — estimated at £388,000 for each of the 766 flats before VAT. RBH said the renovations would add another 50 years to the lifespan of the buildings, while redevelopment would provide 601 homes in a mix of sizes, creating a minimum additional 249 bedrooms, and the properties would last “significantly longer”. Reacting to the news, Greater Manchester Tenants Union said the decision was part of a “managed decline” overseen by the housing provider — a claim RBH denies. GMTU said: “Campaigners and the wider community are very disappointed with the decision to pursue demolition by RBH. “For 10 years the tenants and leaseholders of College Bank have suffered one mistaken decision after another. “RBH claims the decision is based upon ‘a detailed review of all available scenarios’ but it has only allowed for a costing of an overpriced refurbishment plan based upon installing a second staircase in each block of College Bank (under new regulations following the Grenfell disaster).”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A victim of Rochdale grooming gang ringleader Shabir Ahmed has told how she fears he's now living near her - and how she's preparing to move more than 200 miles away as a result. Ahmed - known by his victims as 'Daddy' - was sentenced to 19 years in prison at Liverpool Crown Court in 2012 as one of nine men convicted of offences against five girls. He was released in July after serving 14 years. In a situation that has caused a diplomatic row, the 73-year-old can't be deported because of a 1971 law applying to Commonwealth citizens who arrived in the UK more than 50 years ago. It is being called a 'loophole'. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter Ahmed has been stripped of his British citizenship, leaving him solely as a Pakistani national. Following his release, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said her intention was to change the legal loophole to make it possible to deport those convicted of serious crimes , including terrorism and child sexual exploitation. Pakistan has insisted it will not accept Ahmed's return. Ms Mahmood said the government was preparing to bring forward an ammendment to The Immigration and Asylum Bill because of the case of Ahmed. It went through its third reading in the House of Commons on Tuesday (November 17) and passed by 290 votes to 94. It will now progress to the House of Lords for scrutiny. Sky News interviewed 'Angelina' - not her real name - who told how she was raped by Ahmed as a teenager. She recalled going to a hospital after one attack, but said she was left with 'no support'. "They left me like I was an aninal in the world that you leave in a cage," she said. Ahmed, it is understood, is prevented from being in Rochdale and Greater Manchester as part of his release on licence arrangements. But Angelina said she fears he's been placed 'close' to where she lives. "That's the fear that I have," she said. She said she's now been accepted onto a list to relocate 200 miles away. "I have always got my eyes open at all times because I don't want him to bump into me," she said. The government, meanwhile, has refused to say whether it would impose sanctions on Pakistan to secure Ahmed's deportation.

candidates.source_title: 'I didn't want to move from Seven Sisters flats - but now I'm delighted'
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Andrew Kowalczyk lived on the College Bank estate for 27 years but says he is now happy in his new home After 27 years living in the Seven Sisters tower blocks in Rochdale, Andrew Kowalczyk did not want to leave. But he said he felt the demolition of the flats, which have dominated the town's skyline since the 1960s, was "inevitable" and he was now relieved to have been rehoused. Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) announced last week that the blocks would be bulldozed and replaced with a new College Bank estate of about 600 homes. It comes after a 10-year campaign by residents who wanted the flats to be refurbished and not knocked down but RBH said the demolition was the only "realistic" option. Kowalczyk, 61, who lived in the Mardyke block, said he was reluctant to move out of his "secure" home and the "great views" but he has since been rehomed in a bungalow in Lower Falinge and was now "delighted with it". Residents started to move out of the flats in October last year after long-term safety concerns were raised in October last year. The blocks are almost all empty, with 78 homes out of 766 currently occupied.

candidates.source_title: College showcases new cutting-edge skills hub in historic chapel - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A Grade II-listed former chapel in Middleton has been transformed into a new state-of-the-art engineering and manufacturing training facility. The new facility which opened this month has IT labs and an immersive virtual reality suite based at the landmark Reid building, part of Hopwood Hall College’s Middleton campus. As finishing touches are still being made to the exterior and landscaping, Cllr Sue Smith, cabinet member for communities and co-operation at Rochdale Council was given a preview this week, during a visit arranged to thank the college for its support of Rochdale Feel Good Festival. Hopwood Hall College was one of the main sponsors of this summer’s festival, an event it has supported since 2019, even hosting the main stage at the Rochdale campus in 2022 while the town hall closed for refurbishment. Julia Heap, principal and CEO of Hopwood Hall College, showed Cllr Smith around the site, including a stop at the historic chapel which has been transformed into an innovative skills hub with classrooms, computer labs and a virtual reality suite providing T-Level courses in engineering and manufacturing. Julia Heap, Hopwood Hall College principal and CEO (right) is thanked by Councillor Sue Smith, cabinet member for communities and co-operation at Rochdale Borough Council. Mrs Heap described it as possibly the most unique learning environment in the UK. She said: “This iconic building has always been a favourite with students, staff and college visitors, but now it has a completely new lease of life as a beacon for technical education and skills training while maintaining its character and heritage.

candidates.source_title: Fund helps families struggling to afford school uniforms - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Repair cafes, new hubs for families to buy affordable school uniforms and workshops in upcycling and restoration have all been funded by a scheme to reduce waste and save people money in Greater Manchester. Heywood Uniform Hub CIC is among 19 community groups to receive a total of £200,000 from the Renew Community Fund, supporting community-led projects to keep household items in use for longer, ease pressure on household budgets and bring people together. The increased cost-of-living can make it harder for families to afford everyday essentials such as furniture, electronics, toys and uniforms. At the same time, useful items are often thrown away rather than being passed on or fixed, as the skills needed to mend them have been lost. Now in its sixth year, the Renew Community Fund has awarded a total of £1.3 million to 128 local, community-led projects that help these issues across Greater Manchester. Renew is a joint collaboration between Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) and waste and resources company SUEZ. Money is raised via sales of preloved items that have been donated by Greater Manchester residents at recycling centres. Renew Greater Manchester repairs, refurbishes or upcycles and sells them, with money raised reinvested back into local communities. This year saw a record-breaking number of applications, with a total of 149 projects bidding for funding. READ MORE: New trial will ‘get tough’ with prolific shoplifters

candidates.source_title: Rochdale boss targets areas to ‘hurt’ Cobblers in Sixfields clash
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Both teams go into the game keen for three points to kick-start their respective seasons. Cobblers are 19th in League Two on 15 points, above 22nd-placed Dale on goal difference. “Northampton are coming off the back of a really good result at Salford,” said Watson, who replaced the Stockport-bound Jimmy McNulty in the summer. “I’ve watched that game a couple of times and I thought they played really well. They were robust and they limited Salford. “They are set up really well out of possession, they have good structure and good shape and it’s hard to play through them, so we’ll have to find answers and that’s what we’ve worked on this week. “We’ve looked at where we think we can hurt them and where we can be proactive against them, and also we need to be aware of their strengths. We believe in the group and we believe we can go anywhere and get a result.” Although Rochdale are without a win since early October, Watson was encouraged by their performance in defeat to York City last time out. He added: “We’re really confident we can build on our performance against York. It’s the healthiest we’ve been in terms of selection so we’re in a much better place on that and to get those players back is really positive. Training has been very competitive and everyone is pushing each other. “We need to get better and we need to be more consistent but my belief in this group and in myself has not wavered at all. We’re giving absolutely everything and we’re confident we can put a run of results together.”
candidates.source_summary: Rochdale manager Ian Watson has identified areas that he feels his side can exploit when they face Northampton at Sixfields on Saturday.

candidates.source_title: Springhill Hospice wins three awards including best hospice garden in the North West
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Springhill Hospice in Rochdale has won three awards through the Royal Horticultural Society’s In Bloom programme, including Best Hospice Garden in the North West for 2026. The hospice received Level 5 Outstanding, the highest rating in the Rochdale in Bloom It’s Your Neighbourhood Awards. It also received a Level 5 Outstanding Five Year Achievement Award for maintaining that standard over the five years it has entered. Springhill was named Best Hospice Garden in the North West 2026 at the North West in Bloom Awards. The regional award recognises the role hospice gardens play in providing welcoming spaces for patients, families, visitors and staff. A team of 18 volunteer gardeners maintains the grounds throughout the year. Patients and their loved ones use the gardens to sit together, spend time in quiet surroundings and enjoy the changing seasons. The grounds are also used by visitors, volunteers and staff. Claire Connely, head gardener at Springhill Hospice, said, “I couldn’t be prouder of everyone, but especially our magnificent garden team and all the marvellous things they have achieved together. “Week after week, come rain or shine, our volunteers give their time, skills and energy to care for the gardens and create something truly special for everyone who visits Springhill. “To receive three awards, and particularly to be named Best Hospice Garden in the North West, is wonderful recognition of everything they put into making our gardens what they are. They are an astonishingly beautiful and important part of Springhill, and these awards belong to every person who has played a part in creating and caring for them.” The hospice’s Business Buddies and corporate volunteers regularly contribute their time, expertise and practical help. Local people and organisations donate plant pots, coffee grounds, plants and gardening materials. The team at 3 Pitts allotment grows and donates 400 begonias each spring, which are planted throughout the hospice grounds.

candidates.source_title: Rochdale Masters and Mayfield Movers raise almost £15,000 in two walks
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale Masters Rugby League and Mayfield Movers have raised £14,698.67 for charities and community rugby league through two walking challenges. Their latest walk raised £6,141.80, with three charities set to receive at least £1,500 each. Walkers set off from Ince Rose Bridge ARLFC in Wigan at 6.30am on Saturday 31 October 2026 for the 44-mile All Together Walk. The route took in 10 community rugby league clubs across Greater Manchester, passing through Leigh, Salford and Bury before the group reached Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC at 9.48pm. Volunteers and supporters helped the group during the walk, which took more than 15 hours. Rugby league clubs along the route welcomed the walkers with refreshments and encouragement. The Motor Neurone Disease Association, the Rugby League Cares Brain Health Fund and Springhill Hospice in Rochdale will each receive at least £1,500. The three charities are due to receive a combined minimum of £4,500. Rochdale Masters has committed to covering all fundraising transaction fees so that each charity receives its full allocation. The remaining proceeds will go towards developing the Rochdale Masters section and helping people stay active, socially connected and involved in rugby league. The same groups raised £8,556.87 in October 2025 by walking 52 miles from Rochdale to Blackpool. Mayfield Movers is a community walking group based at Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC, where Rochdale Masters also operates. Both groups aim to help people of different ages, backgrounds and abilities take part in physical activity, build friendships and improve their physical and mental wellbeing.

candidates.source_title: 'Beautiful' boy, 3, who died after police called to nursery in Middleton is named as inquest scheduled - Manchester Evening News
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The three-year-old boy who died after police were called to a nursery in Middleton has been named as Thiago Wall. Thiago tragically died after being rushed to hospital from the Cosy Toes nursery on Mainway East. Emergency crews were called to the nursery on November 2. Pictures from the scene showed a large response with three police vehicles, an ambulance and rapid response paramedic car in attendance. The air ambulance was also pictured landing nearby. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter Sadly, Thiago died in hospital on November 5. His family are being supported by specialist officers. An inquest opening has been scheduled at Rochdale Coroners' Court for November 25. The Cosy Toes nursery has been closed following his death. Greater Manchester Police confirmed an investigation has been launched. Representatives for the nursery described Thiago as a 'wonderful and beautiful child'. A spokesperson for the nursery said: "We are all heartbroken to hear of the tragic news of the child’s passing. "He was a wonderful and beautiful child, and our thoughts and prayers are all with his family at this terrible time. We will of course give our fullest possible assistance in every way possible to the enquiries that must rightly follow this tragic event." Ofsted has suspended the nursery's registration in the wake of the incident, meaning the nursery will be closed for six weeks whilst enquiries are carried out. An Ofsted spokesperson said: "Our thoughts are with the family of the young boy and everyone affected by this deeply distressing incident. "We have worked closely with the police, and we have suspended the nursery's registration. We will continue to support the police and other agencies in their enquiries. We are unable to comment further while the police investigation is ongoing." A GMP spokesperson said no arrests have been made at this stage. "As the circumstances leading up to the boy’s death occurred in a care setting, and in line with usual procedure, a police investigation has been opened", the force spokesperson added. Detective Chief Inspector Claire Brennan said: "This is an incredibly tragic development in a deeply upsetting incident and our thoughts remain with the boy's family. We are in the very early stages of our involvement and are carefully considering events and the evidence available to us.
